hero.subline: ASTRO is the student rocketry association at HVL in Bergen. We design, build, test and launch rockets — the whole cycle, in our own hands.

highlights.heading: From drawing board to launch rail
highlights.lead: Everything we fly is built by students. We design the structure, burn the motors, write the code and head into the field to test — over and over until it flies.

build.title: Structure and propulsion
build.body: Airframes are machined, laminated and assembled in the workshop at HVL. Motors are static-fired on the ground long before anything is cleared to fly.
build.alt: ASTRO students working on the rocket airframe in the workshop

avionics.title: Avionics and electronics
avionics.body: We develop our own flight computer — sensors, logging, telemetry and parachute deployment. Soldered, programmed and tested entirely in-house.
avionics.alt: Close-up of ASTRO's in-house flight computer and electronics

about.heading: Bergen's only rocketry team
about.lead: ASTRO is the student rocketry association at Høgskulen på Vestlandet. We are the only student organisation in Bergen — Norway's second-largest city — building and launching rockets, and we do the whole job ourselves: from the first sketch to motor ignition.
about.heroImageAlt: ASTRO members in the field during a launch outside Bergen

mission.heading: Why we exist
mission.lead: Rocketry is the shortest path from curriculum to practice. ASTRO exists to give students in Western Norway somewhere to use their field for real — with real requirements, real deadlines, and a launch as the final answer.

bergen.title: A rocketry scene in Bergen
bergen.body: Norway's second-largest city had no student rocketry association. Now it has one. We are building the expertise here, instead of students having to leave town to find it.

hands.title: The whole cycle, in our own hands
hands.body: Design, manufacturing, testing, launch and recovery. No part of the rocket is someone else's responsibility — we learn by owning it end to end.

open.title: Open to every student
open.body: We recruit from both HVL and UiB, across every field of study. No rocketry background required — just the urge to build something that actually has to fly.

slogan.caption: The team's slogan — and the benchmark we measure ourselves against every time we head into the field.

story.heading: From idea to first launch
story.imageAlt: ASTRO's rocket on the rail before launch outside Bergen

founding.title: How it started
founding.body: ASTRO was started by students at HVL who wanted to build rockets and found there was nowhere in Bergen to do it. The fix was to build the place themselves: an association, a workshop, and a plan to get something airborne as fast as possible.

firstLaunch.title: The first launch
firstLaunch.body: Our first rocket went up just outside Bergen. Everything from airframe to electronics was built by the members, and the launch gave us what no simulation can: data, mistakes to learn from, and proof that this can be done from here.

today.title: Where we are now
today.body: Today the teams work in parallel on propulsion, structures and avionics. Every launch is documented, every test produces numbers we carry forward — and the ambitions climb with each project.

hybrid.heading: Norway's only student-developed hybrid motor
hybrid.body: ASTRO is the only student organisation in Norway developing a hybrid rocket engine. A hybrid combines solid fuel with a liquid or gaseous oxidiser — it can be throttled and shut down, and it is safer to handle than a pure solid motor. It is also considerably harder to get right, which is rather the point.

design.title: Our own design
design.body: Combustion chamber, injector and nozzle are sized and manufactured by our members.

test.title: Proven on the ground
test.body: The motor runs on an instrumented static test stand before it is cleared to fly.

data.title: Data out of every burn
data.body: Pressure, thrust and temperature are logged and fed straight into the next iteration.

norstec.heading: Connected to NORSTEC
norstec.body: ASTRO is part of NORSTEC, the network tying Norwegian space technology communities together. It connects us to other student groups, gives us access to experience from people who have done this before, and opens a route into the Norwegian space industry for our members.
norstec.aside: For partners, that means supporting ASTRO is also supporting recruitment into a field Norway is investing in.

cta.heading: Want to help build it?
cta.body: We take in new members every semester. Come as you are — we'll teach you the rest.

team.heading: The team
team.lead: ASTRO is run by students from HVL and UiB. The board keeps the association running, while the technical teams build, test and fly the rockets.

board.title: The board
board.body: Responsible for operations, finances, partners and keeping the association running.

propulsion.title: Propulsion
propulsion.body: Motors, propellant and static fires — everything that pushes the rocket upward.

structures.title: Structures
structures.body: Airframe, fins and recovery. The parts that have to survive both launch and landing.

avionics.title: Avionics
avionics.body: Flight computer, sensors, telemetry and the code that runs the flight.

cta.heading: Want to be on this page next year?
cta.body: We take in new members every semester — no rocketry background required, just the urge to build.

partners.heading: Partners and sponsors
partners.lead: Rockets are expensive. What we manage to build, we build because companies, academic groups and suppliers back us with funding, equipment, workshop access and expertise.
